rationale: A Wayland-compatible screenshot annotation tool is a native GUI desktop application problem — it requires deep Linux display server integration that cannot be built with Claude prompts, a web page, and Stripe. The buyer is a Linux hobbyist/developer who strongly prefers free and open-source software, and willingness to pay is very low. This factory has no path to build or deliver a desktop GUI tool autonomously.
solution_plan: This is not a viable build for this factory. A polished Wayland-compatible screenshot/annotation tool is a native desktop application requiring GUI toolkit expertise, Wayland protocol integration, and OS-level packaging — none of which can be produced by Claude plus a landing page. The buyer segment also leans heavily toward free/open-source tools. Recommend dropping entirely.
notes: Fails buildability_with_ai (score 2, floor is 6), operational_autonomy (score 2, floor is 7), buyer_clarity (score 3, floor is 6), and willingness_to_pay (score 3, floor is 5). Total also well below validate threshold.
